current.text: Boston got him in the Jaylen Brown trade.
He is the clear number two option in Boston behind Jayson Tatum. Projected starting lineups include him.
Experts expect his usage to rise from about 23 last season to about 26, in about 32 minutes.
He is healthy. He had no surgery this offseason and comes in fully rested.
Last season he played 37 games. He served a 25-game PED suspension and was coming back from knee surgery. He still finished about 54th per game in category leagues.
Experts expect him to miss some time. They also call the availability fears overdone and expect far more games than last season, possibly double.

Experts project him as a top 40 per game player with top 30 upside. Top 20 is possible with about 34 minutes and 23 points. Over a full season, they put him in the top 40 if he plays about 60 to 65 games.
Experts say his ADP of about 75 to 80 is too low and carries little risk. They would gladly draft him in the 60s and see room for him to beat his rank by up to 50 spots.
In an auction mock he went for 15 USD. The expert would have paid up to 20 USD.
Last season his rim finishing fell from 68 to 57 percent, after three straight seasons above 60.
A recovery to about 63 percent at the rim plus one or two more shots per game would make him a top 40 player.
Boston has 16 back-to-backs, the most in the league, with three of them in our playoff weeks. Its playoff schedule is 4-3-4 games, one short of the maximum.
He is expected to sit some back-to-backs, maybe 8 to 10, but not all of them.
One expert thinks this may be his only season in Boston.

durable.text: He has had knee problems for years. He has also had UCL and shoulder problems.
He served a 25-game PED suspension last season.
His best categories are steals and threes. He is also a strong free throw shooter.
Experts see his game as very fantasy friendly. He adds a little in many categories, he is not just a 3-and-D player, and he can scale his usage up or down.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues.

note: Experts expect a top 40 per game return, but the market prices him as a late flyer: Yahoo average cost is 1.8 USD, ESPN value is 3 USD, and he went for 9 USD in our league last season. Bidding up to Yahoo's 13 USD value, or 15 to 20 USD as in the expert mock, still looks fine. He fits builds that want steals, threes and FT% and can absorb a slightly weak FG%. Early in the season, check his usage as the number two option, how many back-to-backs he sits, and whether his knees hold up.
